narrative.northStar: An office you can disappear into.
narrative.overview: The world leads; the interface is the paperwork carried into it. A generated pixel tower fills the opening, with oversized condensed lettering at the left and Ghost at the right. During play, the camera follows a real character through an isometric office rather than presenting a dashboard of game statistics.
keyCharacteristics: Real pixel artwork, grounded in a playable architectural diorama.
Condensed poster lettering paired with an unobtrusive system UI face.
Warm paper for conversations, mission documents, and deliberate decisions.
Hard-edged, offset depth rather than glass panels or luminous borders.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Status colors reflect actual game state: a completed record, a collected keycard, a delivered concern, or a current connection error.

rules.name: The Voice Rule
rules.body: A speaker's name, portrait, and actual caption establish a conversation. Decoration never replaces those identifiers.

rules.name: The Ground Rule
rules.body: All actor positions and collision decisions come from the engine. Generated ambience, labels, and camera movement cannot change them.

dos: Do keep the office scene dominant and the camera grounded on Ghost.
Do use actual generated artwork with correct proportions and anchors.
Do keep mode, clock, dialogue, and meaningful mission state discoverable.
Do preserve dark focus rings on paper and reduced-motion alternatives.
Do label suspicion as fictional story interpretation.
donts: Don't turn the game into a neon, glass-panel, or metrics dashboard.
Don't make scene art authoritative over collision or navigation.
Don't hide failures behind scripted output labeled as live AI.
Don't encode gaze, accent, facial movements, or emotions as honesty measurements.
Don't replace the committed tower opening or paper documents during a local refinement.
